claims.claim: Researchers using Hubble studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies and found only about 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars remains inside those galaxies today.
claims.episode_span: Researchers using Hubble studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies and measured both retained and lost oxygen across their lifetimes. Only about 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars remains inside these galaxies today, mostly in gas with smaller fractions in stars and dust.
claims.source_title: Nearby Dwarf Galaxies Show Surprising Lack Of Oxygen, Says Paper
claims.supporting_quote: We found that typically 15 percent of the oxygen produced by stars in these low-mass galaxies is still found inside those galaxies today: mostly in their gas, but small fractions are also in the stars and dust, says Telford.

claims.claim: In low-mass galaxies the oxygen-to-hydrogen ratio reaches one atom per 10,000 to 20,000 hydrogen atoms, compared with one per 2,000 in the Milky Way.
claims.episode_span: In these low-mass systems the oxygen-to-hydrogen ratio reaches one atom per 10,000 to 20,000 hydrogen atoms, compared with one per 2,000 in the Milky Way.
claims.source_title: Nearby Dwarf Galaxies Show Surprising Lack Of Oxygen, Says Paper
claims.supporting_quote: In the Milky Way, there is about one oxygen atom for every 2,000 hydrogen atoms, says Telford. In low-mass galaxies like those in the GLOW project, that value is more like one oxygen atom for every 10,000-20,000 hydrogen atoms, she says.

claims.claim: The 8.1-meter Gemini North telescope recorded the highest-resolution view obtained of NGC 7253 or Arp 278 in October 2025.
claims.episode_span: The 8.1-meter telescope recorded the image in October 2025, producing the highest-resolution view obtained of these galaxies.
claims.source_title: Gemini North reveals Twin Spirits in Pegasus
claims.supporting_quote: Three high school students in the Project Hōkūlani internship at Gemini North on Maunakea, Hawaii, chose this pair of clashing spirals, cataloged collectively as NGC 7253 or Arp 278, for imaging with the 8.1-meter telescope. It captured this photo — the most detailed ever taken of these galaxies — in October 2025.
